facts.fact: The museum opened on the island in 2010.

facts.fact: Tate Modern is a London gallery holding the UK national collection of international modern and contemporary art.
facts.quote: Tate Modern is an art gallery in London, housing the United Kingdom's national collection of international modern and contemporary art (created from or after 1900).

facts.fact: The building was originally a power station designed by Giles Gilbert Scott and built in two stages between 1947 and 1963.
facts.quote: This was originally designed by Sir Giles Gilbert Scott, the architect of Battersea Power Station, and built in two stages between 1947 and 1963.

facts.fact: Before conversion it was a long, steel-framed, brick-clad building with a tall central chimney.
facts.quote: Prior to redevelopment, the power station was a 200 m (660 ft) long, steel framed, brick clad building with a substantial central chimney standing 99 m (325 ft).

facts.fact: Herzog & de Meuron won the competition for the conversion, announced in January 1995.
facts.quote: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron of Herzog & de Meuron were announced as the winning architects in January 1995.

facts.fact: The most visible external change was a two-storey glass extension on part of the roof.
facts.quote: The most obvious external change was the two-story glass extension on one half of the roof.

facts.fact: Much of the original interior stayed, including the huge Turbine Hall and its overhead crane.
facts.quote: Much of the original internal structure remained, including the cavernous main turbine hall, which retained the overhead travelling crane.

facts.fact: It was opened by the Queen on 11 May 2000.
facts.quote: Tate Modern was opened by the Queen on 11 May 2000.

facts.fact: It drew 5.25 million visitors in its first year, far more than the older Tate galleries combined the year before.
facts.quote: Tate Modern received 5.25 million visitors in its first year.

facts.fact: The High Line is an elevated linear park on a former railroad spur on the West Side of Manhattan.
facts.quote: The High Line is a 1.45-mile-long (2.33 km) elevated linear park, greenway, and rail trail created on a former New York Central Railroad spur on the West Side of Manhattan in New York City.

facts.fact: Its design is a collaboration between James Corner Field Operations, Diller Scofidio + Renfro and Piet Oudolf.
facts.quote: The High Line's design is a collaboration between James Corner Field Operations, Diller Scofidio + Renfro, and Piet Oudolf.

facts.fact: The abandoned spur was redesigned as a "living system" drawing on landscape architecture, urban design and ecology.
facts.quote: The abandoned spur has been redesigned as a "living system" drawing from multiple disciplines which include landscape architecture, urban design, and ecology.

facts.fact: The park sits on an abandoned southern viaduct section of the New York Central Railroad's West Side Line.
facts.quote: The park is built on an abandoned, southern viaduct section of the New York Central Railroad's West Side Line.

facts.fact: A nonprofit, Friends of the High Line, formed in 1999 to campaign for the structure's preservation and reuse as public space.
facts.quote: A nonprofit organization called Friends of the High Line was formed in 1999 by Joshua David and Robert Hammond, advocating its preservation and reuse as public open space, an elevated park or greenway.

facts.fact: Conversion began in 2006 and the park opened in phases in 2009, 2011 and 2014.
facts.quote: Repurposing the railway into an urban park began in 2006 and opened in phases during 2009, 2011, and 2014.

facts.fact: Since opening it has become an icon of American contemporary landscape architecture and inspired other cities to reuse obsolete infrastructure.
facts.quote: Since opening in June 2009, the High Line has become an icon of American contemporary landscape architecture.

facts.fact: Oudolf's planting relied heavily on native plants, using a matrix of grasses with perennials grouped through it to show how plants grow in the wild.
facts.quote: Oudolf's work on the High Line relied heavily on plants native to the region.

facts.fact: The Pantheon is an ancient Roman temple, originally built under Augustus and reconstructed under Hadrian.
facts.quote: The Pantheon (UK: , US: ; Latin: Pantheum, from Ancient Greek  Πάνθειον (Pantheion) '[temple] of all the gods') is an ancient Polytheist temple in Rome, Italy, originally built under Roman emperor Augustus (27 BC–AD 14) and reconstructed under Hadrian (117–138).

facts.fact: It stands on the site of an earlier temple; the present building was completed by Hadrian and probably dedicated about AD 126.
facts.quote: The Pantheon was built on the site of an earlier temple, which had been commissioned by Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa during the reign of Augustus.

facts.fact: It is round in plan except for a columned portico, with a coffered concrete dome and a central oculus open to the sky.
facts.quote: The building is round in plan, except for the portico with large granite Corinthian columns (eight in the first rank and two groups of four behind) under a pediment.

facts.fact: The dome is still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.
facts.quote: Almost two thousand years after it was built, the Pantheon's dome is still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.

facts.fact: The height to the oculus equals the diameter of the interior circle, so the whole interior would fit exactly within a cube.
facts.quote: The height to the oculus and the diameter of the interior circle are the same, 43.3 metres (142 ft), so the whole interior would fit exactly within a cube (or, a 43.3-m sphere could fit within the interior).

facts.fact: It is among the best-preserved ancient Roman buildings, largely because it has been in continuous use.
facts.quote: It is one of the best-preserved of all Ancient Roman buildings, in large part because it has been in continuous use throughout its history.

facts.fact: Since AD 609 it has served as a Catholic church.
facts.quote: Since AD 609, it has served as the Roman Catholic Basilica of Saint Mary and the Holy Martyrs (Italian: Basilica di Santa Maria ad Martyres) with the special Pontifical privilege of immemorial status.

facts.fact: Its domed circular cella with a conventional temple portico was unique in Roman architecture, yet became a standard model when classical styles were revived.
facts.quote: The Pantheon's large circular domed cella, with a conventional temple portico front, was unique in Roman architecture.

facts.fact: The New Museum of Contemporary Art is at 235 Bowery on Manhattan's Lower East Side.
facts.quote: The New Museum of Contemporary Art is a museum at 235 Bowery, on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in New York City.

facts.fact: The museum opened its new building at 235 Bowery on 1 December 2007, a seven-story facility designed by SANAA with Gensler.
facts.quote: On December 1, 2007, the New Museum opened the doors to its new $50 million location at 235 Bowery, between Stanton and Rivington Streets.

facts.fact: The design was chosen because the building's flexibility and changeable atmosphere match the ever-changing nature of contemporary art.
facts.quote: SANAA's design is chosen because it is in accord with the museum's mission—the flexibility of the building, its changeable atmosphere corresponds to the ever-changing nature of contemporary art.

facts.fact: The stack of white boxes on the Bowery responded to the gentrification of the neighbourhood.
facts.quote: Its decision to put a stack of white boxes on the Bowery was in response to the gentrification of the neighborhood.

facts.fact: In April 2008 the building was named one of the architectural New Seven Wonders of the World by Conde Nast Traveler.
facts.quote: In April 2008, the museum's new building was named one of the architectural New Seven Wonders of the World by Conde Nast Traveler.

facts.fact: The museum is dedicated to introducing new art and new ideas by artists who have not yet received significant recognition.
facts.quote: It is dedicated to introducing new art and new ideas, by artists who have not yet received significant exposure or recognition.

facts.fact: The National Taichung Theater is an opera house in the Xitun District of Taichung, Taiwan.
facts.quote: The National Taichung Theater (Chinese: 臺中國家歌劇院; pinyin: Táizhōng Guójiā Gējù Yuàn; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Tâi-Tiong Kok-Ka Koa-Ke̍k-Īⁿ) is an opera house in the Taichung's 7th Redevelopment Zone in the Xitun District of Taichung, Taiwan.

facts.fact: The structure has an estimated area of 57,685 square metres.
facts.quote: The estimated area of the structure is 57,685 square meters (620,920 sq ft).

facts.fact: Toyo Ito designed it in collaboration with Cecil Balmond at Arup AGU.
facts.quote: It was designed by Japanese architect Toyo Ito in collaboration with Cecil Balmond at Arup AGU.

facts.fact: It was contracted on 11 November 2009 with 45 months of construction planned.
facts.quote: It was contracted on 11 November 2009 with construction planned for 45 months.

facts.fact: It had a partial opening on 23 November 2014 and was officially opened in 2016.
facts.quote: The venue had a partial opening on 23 November 2014.

facts.fact: The Pavilion of Portugal stands in Parque das Nações, Lisbon.
facts.quote: The Pavilhão de Portugal (In English The Pavilion of Portugal ) is a building located in Alameda dos Oceanos, in Parque das Nações, a civil parish in Lisbon, Portugal.

facts.fact: It housed the Portuguese national representation at Expo'98, the 1998 World's Fair.
facts.quote: In the World's Fair in 1998 (Expo'98), the building was responsible for housing the Portuguese National representation at that event.

facts.fact: The entrance is a large square covered by a pre-stressed concrete canopy based on the idea of a sheet of paper resting on two bricks.
facts.quote: The building's entrance area is a large square covered by an imposing pre-stressed concrete canopy, which is based on the idea of a sheet of paper placed on two bricks, opening up space to the city to accommodate the various events that a space of this kind.

facts.fact: After the exhibition the building was left empty and waiting for a use.
facts.quote: After the exhibition, the building was left empty and waiting to be used.

facts.fact: In May 2015 the pavilion was handed over to the University of Lisbon.
facts.quote: In May 2015, the Minister of Environment, Spatial Planning and Energy, Jorge Moreira da Silva, announced that the Pavilion was definitively handed over to the University of Lisbon, which was responsible for its maintenance.

facts.fact: The reuse brings an auditorium for 600 people, exhibition rooms, offices, meeting rooms and a restaurant.
facts.quote: The building will now have an auditorium for 600 people, exhibition rooms, offices, meeting rooms and a restaurant.

facts.fact: Torino Esposizioni is an exhibition hall and convention centre in Turin designed by Pier Luigi Nervi and primarily completed in 1948.
facts.quote: Torino Esposizioni is an exhibition hall and convention centre in Turin, Italy which was primarily completed in 1948, designed by Pier Luigi Nervi.

facts.fact: It is built primarily of ferrocemento and glass.
facts.quote: The building is made with primarily ferrocemento and glass.

facts.fact: Ferrocemento is concrete made in thin cross-sections with metal wire reinforcement and re-usable forms, which Nervi pioneered in Italy and elsewhere.
facts.quote: Ferrocemento is a form of concrete construction made with thin cross-sections of concrete and metal wires (reinforcement) with re-usable forms, which Nervi pioneered in Italy and elsewhere.

facts.fact: For the 2006 Winter Olympics it was converted into a temporary ice rink for ice hockey events.
facts.quote: The Torino Esposizioni was converted into a temporary ice rink to host a number of ice hockey events at the 2006 Winter Olympics along with Palasport Olimpico.

facts.fact: After the Olympics it returned to hosting fairs and exhibitions.
facts.quote: After the Olympics were complete, the arena returned to hosting fairs and exhibitions.

facts.fact: The Roentgen Building is an office building on the Bocconi University campus in Milan.
facts.quote: The Roentgen Building (Italian: Edificio Roentgen) is an office building on the Bocconi University campus in Milan, Italy.

facts.fact: Grafton Architects won a contest organised in 2001 and completed the building in 2008.
facts.quote: The building, ultimated in 2008, was designed by Shelley McNamara and Yvonne Farrell's Grafton Architects, winners of a contest purposefully organized in 2001, as a new office building for Bocconi University.

facts.fact: The building received the World Building of the Year 2008 award.
facts.quote: The building received the World Building of the Year 2008 award.

facts.fact: The exterior is monumental and fortress-like, almost windowless.
facts.quote: The exterior of the building is monumental and fortress-like, being almost windowless.

facts.fact: Jongmyo is a Confucian royal ancestral shrine in Seoul, built in the Joseon period for memorial services for deceased kings and queens.
facts.quote: Jongmyo (Korean: 종묘) is a Confucian royal ancestral shrine in the Jongno District of Seoul, South Korea.

facts.fact: The main buildings were constructed in October 1394 when King Taejo moved the capital to present-day Seoul.
facts.quote: The main buildings of Jongmyo were constructed in October 1394 when Taejo, founder and first king of Joseon, moved the capital to Hanseong (present-day Seoul).

facts.fact: When built in 1394 it was thought to be one of the longest buildings in Asia, if not the longest.
facts.quote: When it was built in 1394 at the order of King Taejo, the Jongmyo Shrine was thought to be one of the longest buildings in Asia, if not the longest.

facts.fact: King Sejong had the Yeongnyeongjeon hall added, and the complex kept growing from west to east as more memorial tablets had to be housed.
facts.quote: The complex was expanded by King Sejong (r. 1418–50) who ordered the construction of Yeongnyeongjeon (영녕전; 永寧殿; lit. 'Hall of Eternal Comfort').

facts.fact: Japanese invaders burned the original shrine in 1592-1598 and a new complex was constructed in 1601, which survives today.
facts.quote: However, during the 1592–1598 Japanese invasions of Korea, Japanese invaders burned down the original shrine and a new complex was constructed in 1601 and has survived to this day.

facts.fact: Each niche is very simple and plain in design.
facts.quote: Each niche is very simple and plain in design.

facts.fact: The current Jeongjeon is a national treasure and the longest building of traditional design in Korea.
facts.quote: The current Jeongjeon is National treasure and is the longest building in Korea of traditional design.

facts.fact: In front of the main hall lies the Woldae Courtyard, 150 metres long and 100 metres wide.
facts.quote: In front of the main hall is the Woldae Courtyard, which is 150 meters in length and 100 meters in width.

facts.fact: Rani ki Vav, the Queen's Stepwell, is a stepwell in the town of Patan in Gujarat, India, on the banks of the Saraswati River.
facts.quote: Rani ki Vav (lit. 'The Queen's Stepwell') is a stepwell situated in the town of Patan in Gujarat, India.

facts.fact: Its construction is attributed to Udayamati, wife of the 11th-century Chaulukya king Bhima I.
facts.quote: Its construction is attributed to Udayamati, the Wife of the 11th-century Chaulukya king Bhima I.

facts.fact: Silted over, it was rediscovered in the 1940s and restored in the 1980s by the Archaeological Survey of India; it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.
facts.quote: Silted over, it was rediscovered in the 1940s and restored in the 1980s by the Archaeological Survey of India.

facts.fact: It is designed as an underground shrine or inverted temple symbolizing the sanctity of water, with sculptures of many Hindu deities.
facts.quote: The stepwell is designed as an underground shrine or inverted temple symbolizing the sanctity of water, with sculptures depicting numerous Hindu deities.

facts.fact: Its seven stair levels carry sculptural panels with more than 500 principal sculptures and over a thousand minor ones.
facts.quote: These panels contain more than 500 principal sculptures and over a thousand minor ones, combining religious, secular, and symbolic imagery.

facts.fact: It measures about 65 metres long, 20 metres wide and 28 metres deep.
facts.quote: It measures approximately 65 metres (213 ft) long, 20 metres (66 ft) wide and 28 metres (92 ft) deep.

facts.fact: Structurally it uses an interlocked post-and-beam system of pillars, columns, walls, brackets and beams to manage vertical loads and lateral soil pressure.
facts.quote: The structural framework of Rani ki Vav uses an interlocked post-and-beam system composed of pillars, columns, walls, brackets and beams designed to manage vertical weight loads and lateral soil pressure.

facts.fact: It was built at the height of artisans' expertise in stepwell construction, in the Maru-Gurjara architecture style.
facts.quote: It was built at the height of artisans’ expertise in stepwell construction and in the Maru-Gurjara architecture style, reflecting mastery of this complex technique and the beauty of its detail and proportions.

facts.fact: The Palestinian Museum is in Birzeit in the West Bank and was inaugurated on 18 May 2016.
facts.quote: The Palestinian Museum is a museum in Birzeit, in the West Bank, Palestine, that was inaugurated on 18 May 2016.

facts.fact: Heneghan Peng was the architectural firm responsible for the building.
facts.quote: The architectural firm responsible for the building was Heneghan Peng, who designed the Grand Egyptian Museum.

facts.fact: The museum building sits atop a terraced hill.
facts.quote: Located atop a terraced hill, the museum building overlooks the Mediterranean.

facts.fact: Its design is inspired by the surrounding rural landscape, so the building integrates into its environment.
facts.quote: With a design inspired by the surrounding rural landscape, the building integrates seamlessly into its environment.

facts.fact: The facade is made of local limestone, and cascading gardens represent the history of Palestinian vegetation and agriculture.
facts.quote: The building's facade is made of local limestone and its cascading gardens represent the history of Palestinian vegetation and agriculture.

facts.fact: Builders laid the terraces by hand, using artisanal knowledge and skill.
facts.quote: Builders laid terraces by hand, incorporating artisanal knowledge and skill.

facts.fact: Outdoor garden spaces extend the interior spaces to allow outdoor exhibitions.
facts.quote: Outdoor garden spaces extend interior spaces to facilitate outdoor exhibitions and blend the building with its environment.

facts.fact: It won the 2019 Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
facts.quote: The Palestinian Museum is notable as a winner of the 2019 Aga Khan Award for Architecture.

facts.fact: The museum's attached Exhibition Hall was designed by I. M. Pei in the late 20th century.
facts.quote: The museum's attached Exhibition Hall was designed by I. M. Pei in the late 20th century.

facts.fact: The museum occupies the 17th-century Zeughaus (armoury) on Unter den Linden, across the Spree from Museum Island.
facts.quote: The museum is located in the 17th-century Zeughaus (armoury) on the Unter den Linden, just across the Spree River from Museum Island.

facts.fact: Pei's new museum hall was built between 1998 and 2003, and glass roofing was installed over the Zeughaus courtyard in the same works.
facts.quote: In the course of the construction of the new adjacent museum hall by I. M. Pei between 1998 and 2003, glass roofing was once more installed above the Schlüterhof

facts.fact: Pei's building has a surface area of 2,700 square metres on four floors, was engineered by Leslie E. Robertson Associates and opened for temporary exhibitions in 2003.
facts.quote: The new building by I. M. Pei with a surface area of 2,700 m2 (29,000 ft2) on four floors, and structurally engineered by Leslie E. Robertson Associates, was opened for temporary exhibitions in 2003.

facts.fact: The Zeughaus is closed for renovation while the Exhibition Hall remains open.
facts.quote: The Zeughaus is closed for renovation, while the Exhibition Hall remains open.

facts.fact: Vancouver House is a neo-futurist residential skyscraper in Vancouver, British Columbia.
facts.quote: Vancouver House is a neo-futurist residential skyscraper in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2016 and completion was postponed to summer 2020.
facts.quote: Construction of the skyscraper began in 2016 and was expected to be finished by the end of 2019, but completion was postponed to summer of 2020.

facts.fact: It was designed by Bjarke Ingels with structural engineers Buro Happold and Glotman Simpson.
facts.quote: Vancouver House was designed by Danish architect Bjarke Ingels and structural engineers Buro Happold and Glotman Simpson.

facts.fact: The design is based on a triangle that rises from the ground and gradually becomes a rectangle at the top.
facts.quote: The design is based on a triangle that rises from the ground and gradually transitions into a rectangle as it ascends to the top.

facts.fact: The form responds to a triangular plot next to the Howe Street on-ramp of the Granville Street Bridge.
facts.quote: The design reflects the constraints of developing the triangular-shaped plot of land immediately east of the Howe Street on-ramp of the Granville Street Bridge.

facts.fact: Box-shaped balconies on the east and west facades give the exterior a honeycomb texture.
facts.quote: The east and west facades of the building feature box-shaped balconies, giving the building's exterior a honeycomb texture.

facts.fact: A public art piece, Spinning Chandelier, was installed nearby as part of the city's rezoning requirement.
facts.quote: Spinning Chandelier, a public art piece, was installed near the skyscraper as part of the city's rezoning requirement.

facts.fact: Flamengo Park is the largest public park in Rio de Janeiro and the largest urban seaside park in the world.
facts.quote: Flamengo Park, also known as Aterro do Flamengo, Eduardo Gomes Park, and Aterro do Brigadeiro Eduardo Gomes, is the largest public park and recreation area within the city of Rio de Janeiro, in eastern Brazil, and the largest urban seaside park in the world. [1]

facts.fact: It lies along Guanabara Bay in the Flamengo neighbourhood, between downtown Rio and Copacabana.
facts.quote: The park is located along Guanabara Bay, in the Flamengo neighborhood of the city, between Downtown Rio and Copacabana.

facts.fact: Lota de Macedo Soares envisioned the park, Affonso Eduardo Reidy conceived and designed it, and Roberto Burle Marx designed its Modernist gardens and civic landscapes.
facts.quote: Flamengo Park was envisioned by Lota de Macedo Soares, while conceived and designed by Affonso Eduardo Reidy with Modernist park gardens and civic landscapes designed by world-renowned landscape designer and artist Roberto Burle Marx.

facts.fact: The 296-acre park was completed in 1965.
facts.quote: The 296 acres (120 ha) park was completed in 1965.

facts.fact: The park was built on land reclaimed from the bay.
facts.quote: The beachfront area is dominated by the Brigadier Eduardo Gomes Park, also known as Aterro do Flamengo, built by Lota de Macedo Soares on nearly 300 acres (1.2 km²) of land reclaimed from the bay and completed in 1965.

facts.fact: The park holds the Rio de Janeiro Museum of Modern Art, the Carmen Miranda Museum and the Monument to the Dead of World War II.
facts.quote: Flamengo Park is the location of the Rio de Janeiro Museum of Modern Art, the Carmen Miranda Museum, and the Monument to the Dead of World War II with Modernist memorial sculptures.

facts.fact: The Palazzo dello Sport (PalaEUR) is a multi-purpose arena in Rome, in the modern EUR complex.
facts.quote: Palazzo dello Sport or PalaEUR, formerly known as PalaLottomatica, is a multi-purpose sports and entertainment arena in Rome, Italy.

facts.fact: Marcello Piacentini designed it in 1957, and Pier Luigi Nervi engineered its reinforced concrete dome.
facts.quote: Palazzo dello Sport was designed by architect Marcello Piacentini, in 1957, and its reinforced concrete dome was engineered by Pier Luigi Nervi.

facts.fact: It was built in two years, 1958 to 1960, in time for the 1960 Summer Olympics.
facts.quote: It was constructed in two years, from 1958 to 1960, in time for the 1960 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: It was built together with a smaller facility, the Palazzetto dello Sport, whose dome Nervi also engineered.
facts.quote: The facility was designed and built along with a smaller facility, the Palazzetto dello Sport, its dome also engineered by Nervi.

facts.fact: The arena hosted the 1960 Olympic basketball tournament.
facts.quote: The arena hosted the 1960 Olympic basketball tournament.

facts.fact: It was renovated between 2000 and 2003 to improve function and acoustics for musical events.
facts.quote: The arena was renovated between 2000 and 2003.

facts.fact: The renovation changed the original look, notably the night lighting of the exterior.
facts.quote: Other changes were made to the original aesthetics of the stadium, particularly the night lighting of its exterior.

facts.fact: Its seating capacity is 11,200 for basketball.
facts.quote: It has a seating capacity of 11,200 spectators for basketball games.

facts.fact: The museum occupies a former school designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh between 1903 and 1906.
facts.quote: It is located in a former school designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh between 1903 and 1906.

facts.fact: Mackintosh based the design on Rowallan Castle in Ayrshire and Falkland Palace.
facts.quote: Mackintosh based the design of the school on Rowallan Castle in Ayrshire and Falkland Palace.

facts.fact: It has a pair of windowed Scottish baronial style tower staircases and a tiled Drill Hall.
facts.quote: The building features a pair of windowed Scottish baronial style tower staircases and a tiled Drill Hall.

facts.fact: The school is an important example of the Modern Style (British Art Nouveau).
facts.quote: The school is an important example of the Modern Style (British Art Nouveau style).

facts.quote: During the building's construction,  Mackintosh frequently battled the school board about the design (the board wanted a less expensive design).

facts.fact: The total cost was £34,291, over budget.

facts.fact: It was designed for 1,250 pupils; the school closed in 1979 and reopened as a museum in 1990.
facts.quote: The school was designed for an enrolment of 1,250.

facts.fact: The building is one of Glasgow's foremost architectural attractions.
facts.quote: The building is one of Glasgow's foremost architectural attractions.

facts.fact: Hyvinkää Church is a modernist Evangelical Lutheran church in Hyvinkää, Finland.
facts.quote: Hyvinkää Church (Finnish: Hyvinkään kirkko, Swedish: Hyvinge kyrka), also known as The New Church of Hyvinkää, is a modernist church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland, located in the town of Hyvinkää, Finland.

facts.fact: Aarno Ruusuvuori designed it and it was built in 1961.

facts.quote: The surface area of the church is 1,779 square metres (19,150 sq ft).

facts.fact: Wide windows light the interior, with a large window behind the altar.
facts.quote: Wide windows produce the lighting, behind the altar is a large window.

facts.fact: Its pyramid-like construction drew some criticism at the time.
facts.quote: The pyramid-like construction caused some criticism at the time.

facts.fact: The mausoleum is a white marble monument over Omar Khayyam's headstone, southeast of Nishapur in Iran.
facts.quote: The Mausoleum of Omar Khayyám (Persian: آرامگاه عمر خیام); is a mausoleum of white marble erected over Omar Khayyám's headstone, located on the south-east of the city of Nishapur, in the northeastern province of Razavi Khorasan, Iran.

facts.fact: It was commissioned by Reza Shah, designed by Hooshang Seyhoun and completed in 1963.
facts.quote: Commissioned by Reza Shah, designed by Hooshang Seyhoun, and completed in 1963, during the Pahlavi era, the structure was added to the Iran National Heritage List on 9 December 1975, administered by the Cultural Heritage, Handicrafts and Tourism Organization of Iran.

facts.fact: It is regarded as a symbol of contemporary Iranian architecture.
facts.quote: The mausoleum is a symbol of contemporary Iranian architecture.

facts.fact: The reconstruction was commissioned by the Iranian government in 1934, during Ferdowsi's millenary.
facts.quote: The reconstruction of the mausoleum was commissioned by the Iranian government under Reza Shah in 1934 during Ferdowsi's millenary.

facts.fact: The tomb was separated from the earlier shrine and the white marble monument was erected over it.
facts.quote: Omar's tomb was separated from the shrine, and a white marble monument, designed by Hooshang Seyhoun, was erected over it.

facts.fact: Seyhoun combined Khayyam's talents as poet, mathematician and astronomer in the design.
facts.quote: Seyhoun combined Khayyam's talents as a poet, mathematician, and astronomer in his design.

facts.fact: A pathway from the garden to the tomb lets flowers fall on it each year, fulfilling Khayyam's wish for a grave adorned with blossoms.
facts.quote: Seyhoun fulfilled this wish by creating a pathway from the garden to Khayyam's tomb, allowing flowers to fall on it annually.

facts.fact: A star-shaped feature on the tomb opens to the sky above Nishapur, honouring Khayyam's geometric work.

facts.fact: The structure is decorated with tiles inscribed with Khayyam poems in calligraphy.

facts.fact: The Teatro General San Martín is an important public theater on Corrientes Avenue in Buenos Aires.

facts.fact: Perón commissioned architects Mario Roberto Álvarez and Macedonio Ruiz to design a new building, and work began on 24 June 1954.

facts.fact: The new building was inaugurated on 25 May 1960, began operating the following year and became one of the most influential cultural centres in Latin America.

facts.quote: Its 30,000 m2 (320,000 sq ft), distributed among thirteen floors and four basements, includes three performance stages, several exhibition halls, and a cinema.

facts.fact: The Italian-style stage has a mouth of variable size and a centre section that can move vertically through nine lifts.
facts.quote: The Italian-style stage is equipped with a mouth of variable sizes (between 11 and 16 metres (36 and 52 ft)) and has a center section that can move vertically, in whole or in part, through nine lifts operating simultaneously or separately.

facts.fact: The theatre and adjacent cultural centre were extensively renovated in 2010-2011.
facts.quote: Both the theater and adjacent cultural center were extensively renovated between 2010 and 2011.

facts.fact: The Temple of Heaven is a complex of imperial Confucian religious buildings in southeastern central Beijing, used for annual prayers to Heaven for a good harvest.
facts.quote: The Temple of Heaven (simplified Chinese: 天坛; traditional Chinese: 天壇; pinyin: Tiāntán) is a complex of imperial religious Confucian buildings situated in the southeastern part of central Beijing.

facts.fact: It was first built in 1420 under the Yongle Emperor of the Ming dynasty and later expanded and reconstructed.
facts.quote: The temple complex was first built in 1420, during the reign of the Yongle Emperor of the Ming dynasty, who was also responsible for the construction of the Forbidden City in Beijing.

facts.fact: The present layout was largely formed by 1749 after Qing-period reconstruction.
facts.quote: The present layout of the complex was largely formed by 1749, following Qing-period reconstruction.

facts.fact: The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is a triple-gabled circular building 36 m across and 38 m tall, on three levels of marble base.
facts.quote: The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests (祈年殿) is a triple-gabled circular building, 36 m (118 ft) in diameter and 38 m (125 ft) tall, built on three levels of marble stone base, where the Emperor prayed for good harvests.

facts.fact: That hall is built entirely of wood, with no nails.
facts.quote: The building is completely wooden, with no nails.

facts.fact: The Imperial Vault of Heaven is surrounded by a smooth circular Echo Wall that can transmit sounds over large distances.
facts.quote: It is surrounded by a smooth circular wall, the Echo Wall, that can transmit sounds over large distances.

facts.fact: Earth was represented by a square and Heaven by a circle, and several features symbolize the connection of the two.
facts.quote: Earth was represented by a square and Heaven by a circle; several features of the temple complex symbolize the connection of Heaven and Earth, of circle and square.

facts.fact: The outer wall has a taller semi-circular north end representing Heaven and a shorter rectangular south end representing Earth.
facts.quote: The whole temple complex is surrounded by two cordons of walls; the outer wall has a taller, semi-circular northern end, representing Heaven, and a shorter, rectangular southern end, representing the Earth.

facts.fact: The Circular Mound Altar is laid out in nines, since nine represents the Emperor.
facts.quote: The number nine represents the Emperor and is evident in the design of the Circular Mound Altar: a single round marmor plate is surrounded by a ring of nine plates, then a ring of 18 plates, and so on for a total of nine surrounding rings, the outermost having 9×9 plates.

facts.fact: All the buildings have dark blue roof tiles, representing Heaven.
facts.quote: All the buildings within the Temple have special dark blue roof tiles, representing the Heaven.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier designed it for King Faisal II in 1956, for potential use in the 1960 Summer Olympics; after the 1958 coup the project underwent several design and location changes.
facts.quote: Designed by Le Corbusier under the commission of King Faisal II in 1956 for potential use in the 1960 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier left drawings for a whole sports complex, but only the gymnasium was finally built, between 1978 and 1980.
facts.quote: Le Corbusier died in 1965, leaving a wealth of drawings and studies for the multi-functions of Baghdad's Sports Complex which included a large stadium, tennis courts, swimming pools, and a gymnasium.

facts.fact: The building is constructed of reinforced concrete.
facts.quote: The center is constructed of reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: The main roof spans 34 metres on a steel truss covered with corrugated aluminum sheets.
facts.quote: The main roof spans 34 metres and is constructed with a steel truss covered with corrugated aluminum sheets.

facts.fact: The trusses are exposed inside and house the mechanical ducts.
facts.quote: The trusses are exposed in the interior and house the mechanical ducts.

facts.fact: An enormous sliding door links the indoor 3,000-seat hall and the adjacent open-air amphitheater so they can be opened into one space.
facts.quote: The indoor 3,000 seat stadium and the adjacent open-air amphitheater are linked by an enormous sliding door which, when opened, integrates the two stadia.

facts.fact: King Faisal II invited many Western architects, Le Corbusier among them, as part of a plan to modernize Greater Baghdad.
facts.quote: The King invited many Western architects, among them was Le Corbusier who would go on to design the Baghdad Gymnasium.

facts.fact: The World Forum is a concert venue and convention centre in The Hague, originally called Nederlands Congresgebouw.
facts.quote: The World Forum (originally known as Nederlands Congresgebouw and formerly Nederlands Congres Centrum and World Forum Convention Center) is a concert venue and convention centre in The Hague, Netherlands, near the buildings of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) and one of the administrative offices of the International Baccalaureate.

facts.fact: It opened in 1969, designed in the Dutch functionalism style by J. J. P. Oud.
facts.quote: It was opened in 1969 and was designed in the Dutch functionalism style by architect Jacobus Johannes Pieter Oud.

facts.fact: Oud's son Hans Oud completed construction after his father's death in 1963.
facts.quote: His son, Hans Oud, completed the construction after his father's death in 1963.

facts.fact: In 2006 part of the convention centre, including the Statenhal, was demolished to make way for the Europol building.
facts.quote: In 2006 a part of the convention center, including the Statenhal, was demolished to make place for the Europol building.

facts.fact: It hosted the North Sea Jazz Festival and the Eurovision Song Contests of 1976 and 1980.
facts.quote: Many concerts and festivals had been held there before, such as the annual North Sea Jazz Festival, and the Eurovision Song Contests of 1976 and 1980.

facts.fact: Grieg Hall is a 1,500-seat concert hall on Edvard Griegs plass in Bergen, Norway.
facts.quote: Grieg Hall (Norwegian: Grieghallen) is a 1,500-seat concert hall located on Edvard Griegs plass (square) in Bergen, Norway.

facts.fact: It is named after the Bergen-born composer Edvard Grieg and is home to the Bergen Philharmonic Orchestra.
facts.quote: Grieghallen was named in honor of Bergen-born composer Edvard Grieg, who served as music director of the Bergen Philharmonic Orchestra from 1880 until 1882.

facts.fact: The Danish architect Knud Munk designed it in a modernist style.
facts.quote: The building was designed in a modernist architecture style by the Danish architect Knud Munk.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1967 and finished by May 1978.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1967 and was finished by May 1978.

facts.fact: It is used each year for concerts, ballet and opera, and is also a conference and exhibition centre.
facts.quote: Grieghallen is used each year for a series of concerts, ballet and opera performances.

facts.fact: It hosted the Eurovision Song Contest in 1986.
facts.quote: It hosted the Eurovision Song Contest in 1986, the Eurovision Young Musicians in 2000, and is the host of the annual Norwegian Brass Band Championship competition, which occurs in mid-winter.

facts.fact: The Peak Tower is a shopping complex at Victoria Gap near the summit of Victoria Peak, housing the upper terminal of the Peak Tram.
facts.quote: The Peak Tower is a shopping complex located at Victoria Gap, near the summit of Victoria Peak on Hong Kong Island, Hong Kong.

facts.fact: The architects wanted a prominent design that would not interrupt the natural line of the hills, so they chose a site in a dip and limited the height.
facts.quote: Because the architects sought a design which would be prominent on the skyline but would not interrupt the natural line of the hills, they chose a site in a dip along the line of the hills, and restricted the tower's height to 428 m above sea level.

facts.fact: The current tower is the second on the site; the first, by Chung Wah Nan, opened in 1972.
facts.quote: The current Peak Tower is the second on the site.

facts.fact: In the first tower the upper floors were carried on two columns, leaving clear space between the upper and lower parts, a feature kept in the new tower.
facts.quote: Both the upper floors were supported by two columns allowing a clear space between the upper and lower parts of the tower.

facts.fact: The first tower was demolished in 1993 and work on the new one began that year.
facts.quote: The first tower was demolished in 1993 and a groundbreaking ceremony on the new tower was held later the same year.

facts.fact: The current tower is by Terry Farrell, completed in 1997, with seven floors and a wok shape at the top.
facts.quote: The current Peak Tower was the work of the British architect Terry Farrell, and was completed in 1997.

facts.fact: From 2005 to 2006 the lower portion was glassed in to add retail space and the escalators were relocated.
facts.quote: The building was altered from 2005–2006 at a cost of $100 million.

facts.fact: The viewing terrace now sits at the top of the wok shape, overlooking Victoria Harbour.
facts.quote: The Peak Tower now has eight floors with the viewing terrace relocated to the top of the building (at the top of the 'wok' shape) that overlooks both Victoria Harbour and Aberdeen (SW of the Hong Kong Island); however, severe air pollution often hinders the outlook from this venue.
